title: Stochastic resonance
description: A double well that tilts slowly back and forth, $\Psi(t, x, y) = \frac{(x^2 - 4)^2}{16} + \frac{y^2}{2} + \frac{3x}{20}\sin\left(\frac{t}{5}\right)$. The tilt alone is too weak to push particles over the barrier; noise does that. The Observable window shows the fraction of particles in the right well, $P(X^1_t > 0)$. Try σ = 0.5, 0.8 and 1.2 (restart the scenario in between and change σ).

questions.text: What is the period of the forcing?
At σ = 0.5, do the particles follow the tilt? Describe the curve.
At which σ does the fraction in the right well follow the forcing most regularly?
Explain with Kramers' law why too little and too much noise both destroy the synchronisation.
